claims.value: Bodart: side A (French) 13,000 infantry and 4,500 cavalry, total 17,500; side B (Spanish) 20,000 infantry and 3,000 cavalry, total 23,000.

claims.rationale: Claim-relevant rendering; this printed label does not establish continuous field presence or a sole credited commander. English rendering (ours): "French-side command: Victor; opponent-side command: Cuesta."

claims.value: The frozen frame records side A as Bodart’s winner.
claims.rationale: Source convention frozen; outcome is not a causal attribution or evidence of skill. English rendering (ours): "Bodart places side A first, his recorded victor."

claims.value: Toreno gives side B 20,000 infantry and 2,000 cavalry brought to the Medellin field by Cuesta.
claims.rationale: Field population; cavalry alternative to Bodart retained, not averaged. English rendering (ours): "Cuesta brought his men there, 20,000 infantry and 2,000 cavalry."

claims.value: Toreno gives side A 18,000 infantry and nearly 3,000 cavalry under Victor.
claims.rationale: Spanish opponent estimate, separate from Bodart’s available-force convention. English rendering (ours): "The total was 18,000 infantry and nearly 3,000 cavalry; Marshal Victor commanded in chief."

claims.value: Jourdan estimates side B at about 30,000 combatants in its deployed army.
claims.rationale: Interested French estimate of the opposing army, not Cuesta’s own return. English rendering (ours): "This army counted about 30,000 combatants."

claims.value: Jourdan places Villatte in the French centre and Ruffin in reserve, within Victor’s operation.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Villatte’s division, with the remaining German division on its left, was placed in the centre; Ruffin’s formed the reserve."

citations.locator: jourdan, printed p. 184, Internet Archive leaf 201; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: La division Villatte, ayant à sa gauche le reste de la division allemande, fut placée au centre. Celle de Ruffin forma la réserve.

claims.value: Toreno places the Spanish left under Henestrosa and del Parque, and the right-hand combined force under Eguía.
claims.rationale: Contingent offices under Cuesta; Zayas’s effective vanguard role is separately described in the following page and remains a deferred authority detail. English rendering (ours): "The vanguard and first division were under Henestrosa and del Parque; the [right-hand combined] corps was governed by Lieutenant General Francisco de Eguía."

claims.value: Jourdan describes the Spanish main army advancing to meet the French army after Cuesta brought it onto the ridge.
claims.rationale: Main offensive movement described here, not inferred merely from a local countercharge; the French crossing and deployments do not by themselves prove a second main offensive. English rendering (ours): "The Spaniards advanced boldly toward the French army and the action soon became very lively."

citations.locator: jourdan, printed p. 184, Internet Archive leaf 201; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Les Espagnols se portèrent avec beaucoup d’intrépidité au-devant de l’armée française, et l’action ne tarda pas à devenir des plus vives.

claims.value: Toreno describes an open treeless plain between the river bed, Don Benito and Mingabril.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "A broad treeless plain opens between the river bed, Don Benito and Mingabril."
